source_references.title: PwC deploys Microsoft Copilot at enterprise scale: PwC

business_problem: PwC needed to deploy generative AI across a global network in a way that improved everyday productivity while preserving local compliance, strong governance, and enterprise security.
solution_summary: PwC turned Microsoft Copilot into a governed enterprise AI layer rather than a standalone productivity pilot. Working with Microsoft, the firm embedded Copilot into the Microsoft 365 environment its people already use, then rolled it out across more than 100 countries using a decentralized operating model. Territory teams could choose configurations that matched local regulatory and operational needs, while a hub-and-spoke governance model, global knowledge center, and sharing framework kept standards consistent. PwC also built dashboards from Microsoft data sources to track adoption, usage, efficiency gains, and behavior across Teams, Outlook, and later Copilot Studio agent reporting. Role-based training, prompt campaigns, and feedback loops refined how agents and features were used in practice. The result is one of the world’s largest Copilot deployments, with Responsible AI, local data controls, and enterprise security built into the rollout rather than bolted on later.

solution_components.name: Microsoft Copilot
solution_components.role: Acts as the primary AI assistant embedded across PwC’s day-to-day work environment.

solution_components.name: Microsoft 365
solution_components.role: Provides the enterprise productivity environment into which Copilot was deployed at scale.

solution_components.name: Microsoft Teams
solution_components.role: Supplies collaboration context and one of the main applications where Copilot usage is monitored.

solution_components.name: Microsoft Outlook
solution_components.role: Provides communication context and another primary surface for Copilot adoption and workflow integration.

solution_components.name: Copilot Studio
solution_components.role: Supports the evolution of agent reporting and the next layer of Copilot-based automation.

data_flow: Work content and Microsoft-provided data sources remain inside PwC’s Microsoft 365 estate, where Microsoft Copilot surfaces assistance within Teams, Outlook, and related applications. Usage and adoption data feed PwC-built dashboards, and local territory configurations plus governance controls determine how agents and features are deployed across the global network.
business_outcome: PwC operationalized one of the world’s largest Copilot deployments, generating more than 20 million monthly actions, over 1 million hours of capacity in one month, and a governed foundation for ongoing AI adoption across the network.

architecture_clues: The rollout began in 11 countries using a decentralized model.
A hub-and-spoke governance model balanced territory autonomy with global standards.
PwC built dashboards to monitor Teams, Outlook, and other Microsoft application usage.
Role-based training included prompt-of-the-day campaigns and responsible-AI guidance.
evidence_quotes: With over 285,000 users in 100+ countries, we have built one of the world’s largest Copilot deployments—driving productivity, enhancing collaboration, and embedding trust throughout multiple workflows.
During the month of April 2026, PwC employees executed over 20M million actions in Copilot, freeing up over 1M hours of capacity in the process.
With 54% of PwC’s global workforce using AI tools weekly, employees average nine prompts per week.
AI agents now help research teams extract data from complex files in seconds, freeing PwC employees to focus on higher-value insights.
Today, Copilot isn’t just an assistant. It’s an integrated AI framework that powers smarter, faster, and more trusted work—for PwC and for our clients.
